review_cost.rationale: I'd approve after one round of nits: bound the cache, dedupe the team-cookie logic, add API types. Nothing requires structural rework.

findings.issue: In-memory cache Map never evicts entries (only rejected fetches are deleted) and keys include user-controlled path segments; 404 nulls are cached too, so a long-running server grows the map without bound.
findings.suggestion: Cap the cache (Astro 7's memoryCache({max}) is LRU for a reason) or drop 404s from the cache and bound keys to a whitelist.

findings.issue: Team-cookie read/write logic is duplicated from app/src/lib/team.ts and doesn't apply the same validation rules (regex, length cap), so the two implementations can drift.
findings.suggestion: Define the cookie format once (a small shared module or at least a single well-documented spec) and have both sides reference the same constraints.

findings.issue: Client-side results swap doesn't check res.ok; on a server error the URL has already been updated but the DOM is unchanged (same pattern in MovesSection.astro:192-200).
findings.suggestion: Check res.ok and fall back to location.assign(url), as the catch branch already does for network errors.

findings.issue: SWR background refresh failures are silently swallowed and the stale entry is re-marked fresh, so errors from the API are invisible.
findings.suggestion: Log or count refresh failures and don't bump the timestamp on failure.

findings.issue: One module owns species, types, generations, cards, team members and coverage; every page depends on it and any refactor touches everything.
findings.suggestion: Split into per-domain modules (species, types, moves, team) behind the existing function names, or at least keep new domains out.

findings.issue: Pervasive `any` for API records (16 hits across the app) with no shared type definitions; typos in property names would surface only at runtime.
findings.suggestion: Add a types module for the handful of API records actually used (species, pokemon, type, move, ability).

findings.issue: All ~550 lines of CSS live in global stylesheets; no component uses Astro's scoped <style>, so class names are the only boundary between components.
findings.suggestion: Move component-specific rules (card, evolution, moves table) into scoped styles in their components.

findings.issue: Cold-cache Pokémon page fans out one request per learnable move (often 100+) plus one per version group before rendering.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable given the concurrency limiter and 60s cache, but consider a shorter review timeout or batched rendering of the moves table.

summary: A clean, current-idiom Astro 7 SSR app whose routing, 404 handling and progressive enhancement I'd happily merge after nits. The two things I'd insist on before long-term ownership are bounding the request cache and deduplicating the team-cookie logic between server and client. Everything else is polish: shared API types and scoped component styles.
